title: CI is far too tedious
summary: A PR that is approved and passes the CI can take days to merge. If other PRs cut the queue and get merged while the CI is rebuilding things for the $n$-th time, the PR needs to manually be inspected for the $n+1$-th iteration of merging main and re-running everything from scratch. This is wasteful of time and wasteful of resources. Occasionally all PRs become blocked when resource limits are exceeded. Worse, there seems to be little reason for it. If the changes are tested and pass the tests and do not conflict with merges that keep cutting the queue, then they could just be merged into main without rerunning all the tasks for the $n+2$-th time.
